Subject: Recap + next steps: privacy alignment, DPA request & SCC module preference

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on timeline and responsibilities: 

Call highlights
- MedSys uses Redwood for inference in production (token-based throughput) and has EU and US data flows.
- MedSys requires confirmation of our SOC 2 status and wants to initiate a formal VSQ and DPA conversation.
- Primary compliance asks: SOC 2 Type II report, confirmation of role under GDPR (controller vs processor), SCC module preference, and HIPAA applicability for PHI use-cases.

Redwood position (summary)
- Redwood acts as a data processor for customers using our hosted and dedicated products; customers remain the data controller. If there are any specific features where control shifts, we will call that out explicitly in the DPA.
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II in scope; will share the summary report and auditor letter under NDA.

Proposed next steps (owned by party)
1) MedSys: please share the completed vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) and indicate whether you treat Redwood as processor for this engagement. (Owner: MedSys — Tom/Sarah)
2) Redwood: share our DPA draft and recommended SCC module (we typically recommend the Controller→Processor module for EU exports). I attached the initial DPA draft for your review. (Attachment: redwood_dpa_v1.docx) (Owner: Redwood — Mina)
3) MedSys: flag any HIPAA-specific requirements or dataflows that need special handling and timeline for SOC 2 evidence review. (Owner: MedSys)
4) Timeline: propose internal review by 10/29 and a follow-up call week of 11/2 to finalize SCC choice and DPA redlines.

Attachments included: redwood_dpa_v1.docx

If that looks right I’ll kick off the DocuSign flow for a clean DPA signature once MedSys confirms the controller/processor role and SCC choice.

Thanks — Mina

--

Thanks Mina — good summary. Appreciate the clear next steps. Attaching our completed VSQ and a short note on the MedSys expectations below. (Attachment: MedSys_VSQ.xlsx)

Quick answers / clarifications
- We are treating Redwood as a processor for the integration (our legal team expects a standard processor DPA).
- For SCCs, our EU privacy team typically asks for the Controller→Processor module; we’ll confirm but that aligns with our norm.
- HIPAA: we do ingest Limited Data Set PHI in a small number of workflows. We need to confirm that Redwood’s processing environment and logging meet our HIPAA BA requirements. If you have a HIPAA addendum we can review that in parallel.
- SOC 2: we require the auditor letter and the most recent Type II report. We can sign an NDA to receive the full report.

Next steps from our side
- I’ll route the VSQ to InfoSec and Legal; expect feedback by 10/28.
- If possible, can you include a short note in the DPA about subprocessor notification timing? That’s a sticking point for us.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the fast turnaround and for attaching the VSQ. A few clarifications and commitments from our side: 

1) Processor confirmation & DPA edits
- Confirming Redwood will be the processor for this engagement. We will send a processor-focused DPA. I have attached a PDF version of our processor DPA for quicker review (redwood_processor_dpa_v1.pdf).
- We will add explicit subprocessor notification timing language (we typically provide 30 days’ notice for new subprocessors; we can scope this to your preference).

2) SCC module recommendation
- Based on the call and your note, we recommend the Controller→Processor module (the standard module used for data exports from the EEA to processors). We’ll mark that in the DPA and provide a redline showing the SCC module selection.

3) SOC 2 and HIPAA
- SOC 2: we can share the auditor letter and redacted Type II report under NDA. I’ll send a DocuSign NDA link immediately after this message if that speeds things up.
- HIPAA: we have a HIPAA addendum template; if MedSys confirms specific BA requirements we’ll highlight any operational controls to ensure alignment (logging, encryption, access controls).

Attachments & links
- redwood_processor_dpa_v1.pdf (attached)
